acceptance: An ADR defines each terminal and non-terminal outcome, including completed, failed, timed_out, cancel_requested, outstanding_work, publishing, and unknown, and states which outcomes may carry valid benchmark metrics.

A producer-to-consumer inventory names every in-scope scheduler, wrapper, combined runner, result serializer, and durable-job transition, with one owner for cancellation, resource cleanup, and final status publication.
The contract distinguishes bounded caller response from actual work termination; a returned timeout cannot imply that database work stopped.
The contract states when later phases or resource reuse are forbidden and defines the evidence required to lift that prohibition.

The decision reconciles the current throughput runner, TPC-DI enhanced pipeline, expected-results registry, execution-manager APIs, MCP durable jobs, and relevant open or completed tracker items without silently superseding them.
No implementation is permitted to claim universal cancellation, exactly-once execution, or production readiness unless the chosen contract and proving tests establish that property.
context: Problem reframe: the core issue is not thread-count support. It is truthful status and exclusive ownership across asynchronous boundaries. Extend existing narrow state machines where possible; do not introduce a second orchestration framework. This item is the prerequisite for the implementation branches below.
description:
BenchBox has several concurrent execution paths, but they do not share a precise contract for completed, failed, timed-out, cancelled, still-running, publishing, and unknown outcomes. Define the smallest common vocabulary and ownership rules needed to prevent false success, invalid metrics, unsafe phase overlap, and duplicate durable work. This is a contract and decision item, not a broad executor rewrite.

Decision boundary: adopt one shared outcome model only where the same semantics are real; otherwise define explicit adapters between narrower contracts. Record the choice in an ADR because it affects public result meaning and durable-job compatibility. Reconcile current code, documentation, and tracker decisions before implementation starts.
